attrs.rationale: Warm pools avoid cold-start latency while preserving sterile, deterministic execution environments.
ForgeHarbor is stateful, unlike ForgeAtlas, and must manage live containers, background reconciliation, heartbeats, and graceful shutdown.
Defines ForgeHarbor as a long-running daemon with Pool Manager, Lifecycle Engine, Heartbeat Monitor, and Provider Interface.
Builds pure lifecycle logic first, then provider, pool, daemon, and Docker packaging.
Prioritizes transition guard, lifecycle functions, provider contract, PoolManager, and assignment lock as P0 dependencies.

reconcile, assignment, release, max environments, pool status
healthy checks, failed ASSIGNED/WARMING detection, start/stop loop
daemon startup, shutdown, API wrappers, health
Docker provision, health, terminate, connection info
end-to-end daemon lifecycle against real Docker

attrs.rationale: Pre-provisioned environments let agent sessions bind immediately rather than waiting for cold container startup.
Pool management should not change when DockerProvider is replaced by a future KubernetesProvider.
Caller-facing functions use the same ok/error convention as ForgeAtlas and ForgeWorks.
ForgeHarbor manages the container-level isolation that DAWN executes inside.
The packaging plan uses a Docker socket mount so ForgeHarbor manages sibling containers rather than running Docker-in-Docker.
